scope: Native Linux i386 SVM address widths in NeverC and both NeverD C routes, including exact i386 addr16 and x64 addr32 assembly fallbacks
r6_compatibility: Exact assembly fallback and explicit refusal of unregistered VMXOFF declarations; no claim that r6 supplies the new native IDs

immutable_table_review.change: Existing immutable metadata entry, x86 count1815 to1821 only; no new allowlist entries or relaxed matchers.

observations: The effective address size selects the implicit rAX input.
INVLPGA retains a full ECX ASID.
VMLOAD/VMSAVE use system-physical VMCB addresses; INVLPGA uses a linear address.
reference.limitation: Mirror of a primary AMD manual, not a successful fetch of the current AMD-hosted revision.

limits: Linux i386 uses the full LLVM backend; the embedded backend clearly rejects the new i386 intrinsic IDs.
Windows and Darwin i386 native source ABI qualification remains open.
Stopped-instruction comparisons verify source transport and ABI, not privileged SVM or VMX execution.
QEMU TCG VMCB/MSR, interrupt and VMRUN results do not establish physical AMD TLB invalidation or hardware VM entry.
The complete-C witnesses use flat segment bases; nonzero VMX bases and truncation belong to the separate address witness.
Full real/VM86/IA-32e transitions, task switching, remaining state banks, software SMM/SGX and unbound asynchronous producers remain open.
The strict source-global audit is unchanged from its 90-finding baseline, not a clean global gate.
The AMD reference is a mirror of revision 3.26; the current AMD-hosted revision was unavailable.
